cards.back: A positive integer is divisible by 2 iff its units digit is even (0,2,4,6,8).
A positive integer is divisible by 5 iff its units digit is 0 or 5.

cards.front: State and prove the divisibility rule for 3.
cards.back:
N is divisible by 3 iff the sum of its decimal digits is divisible by 3.
Proof: since $10\equiv1\pmod{3}$, we have $N\equiv\sum d_i\pmod{3}$.

cards.front: State and prove the divisibility rule for 4.
cards.back:
N is divisible by 4 iff the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4.
Proof: $100\equiv0\pmod{4}$, so $N\equiv10d_1+d_0\pmod{4}$.
N is divisible by 6 iff it is divisible by both 2 and 3 (i.e., last digit even and digit sum divisible by 3).

cards.front: State and prove the divisibility rule for 9.
cards.back:
N is divisible by 9 iff the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.
Proof: $10\equiv1\pmod{9}$, hence $N\equiv\sum d_i\pmod{9}$.

cards.front: State and prove the divisibility rule for 8.
cards.back:
N is divisible by 8 iff the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8.
Proof: $1000\equiv0\pmod{8}$, so only the last three digits matter.

cards.front: State and prove the divisibility rule for 11.
cards.back:
N is divisible by 11 iff the alternating sum of its digits is divisible by 11 (including 0).
Proof: $10\equiv-1\pmod{11}$, so $N\equiv\sum(-1)^k d_k\pmod{11}$.
